_comment: REAL CONTENT, NOT STEWARD-APPROVED. Transcribed from the scanned Prakas PDFs published by the National Bank of Cambodia at https://www.nbc.gov.kh/english/legislation/prakas_new.php, read on 2026-07-31. Unlike the MPWT corpus, these chunks carry REAL ARTICLE NUMBERS, because the article text itself was read rather than a service page summarising it.
_translationNote: CRITICAL. Both source PDFs are stamped 'Unofficial Translation' by the NBC itself. The English below is the NBC's own unofficial English rendering, not the authoritative Khmer text. A citizen relying on an exact figure or deadline should be pointed to the Khmer original. This is recorded in each `doc` value so it reaches the citation, not just this comment.
_noKhmerNote: `textKm` is deliberately absent on every chunk. The NBC publishes these documents as scanned images and the Khmer originals were not read. Machine-translating the English back into Khmer would manufacture a Khmer 'source text' that no ministry ever wrote — the exact failure this corpus exists to avoid. Khmer retrieval for these chunks therefore rests on the Khmer keywords and questions only, which is a known and accepted recall gap, not an oversight.
_dateNote: The NBC listing page dates the consumer complaints Prakas 'October 25, 2018', but the document itself is signed 'Phnom Penh, September 27, 2017'. The document's own date is used. The discrepancy is likely a site upload date and is recorded here rather than silently resolved.
_scopeNote: The NBC legislation page carries 162 Prakas, Circulars and Announcements. The overwhelming majority are prudential rules addressed to banks — capital adequacy, reserve requirements, liquidity ratios, chart of accounts — which a citizen never needs and which would dilute retrieval. Only the consumer-facing instruments were taken. The remainder belong in sources.json as monitored material, not in the answering corpus.

chunks.doc: Prakas on Resolution of Consumer Complaints (NBC unofficial English translation)
chunks.instrument: Prakas No. B7-017-299 Prokor dated 27 September 2017 on Resolution of Consumer Complaints
chunks.text: A bank, microfinance institution or other institution under the supervisory authority of the National Bank of Cambodia is required to receive and resolve each complaint lodged by a consumer or their representative, including complaints forwarded by the National Bank of Cambodia. A consumer must file a complaint within 60 days after becoming aware of the problem the complaint is based on. A complaint may be lodged in writing or verbally. The institution must not impose any restriction that would discourage consumers from lodging complaints or limit their right to do so, including imposing any cost on the consumer for filing, processing or disposing of the complaint.

chunks.doc: Prakas on Resolution of Consumer Complaints (NBC unofficial English translation)
chunks.instrument: Prakas No. B7-017-299 Prokor dated 27 September 2017 on Resolution of Consumer Complaints
chunks.text: A complaint lodged verbally must be resolved within 2 working days. Where it cannot be resolved in that time, the institution must ask the consumer or their representative to lodge the complaint in writing. Where a consumer wants to file a written complaint but is unable to do so for any reason, the institution must document the complaint on the consumer's behalf, file it through its complaint management process, and give the consumer a copy of the complaint document. For a written complaint, the institution must issue a complaint receipt as soon as the complaint is received. The receipt must show at least the registration number, the date the complaint was received, the name of the consumer or representative, the name and telephone number of the staff member who received it, and a brief description of the complaint, and must be signed by the staff member who received it. The institution must then complete its fact finding within a maximum of 30 calendar days from the date the receipt was issued, and must notify the consumer in writing of the result with clear reasons. Where a decision is not issued within 30 calendar days, the institution must inform the consumer of the delay and the reasons for it.

chunks.doc: Prakas on Resolution of Consumer Complaints (NBC unofficial English translation)
chunks.instrument: Prakas No. B7-017-299 Prokor dated 27 September 2017 on Resolution of Consumer Complaints
chunks.text: For the purposes of this Prakas, a consumer is any natural person who is seeking a product or service from an institution or who has an existing consumer relationship with an institution. A complaint is a consumer's expression of dissatisfaction with a product or service offered or provided by the institution. A Senior Consumer Relation Officer is a senior manager of an institution, appointed by the board of directors, who manages the institution's Consumer Complaint Management Framework. The institution must send the name and contact information of its Senior Consumer Relation Officer to the National Bank of Cambodia, and must notify the National Bank of Cambodia immediately if that officer changes.

chunks.doc: Prakas on Resolution of Consumer Complaints (NBC unofficial English translation)
chunks.instrument: Prakas No. B7-017-299 Prokor dated 27 September 2017 on Resolution of Consumer Complaints
chunks.text: An institution that fails to comply with this Prakas is penalised under Article 52 of the Law on Banking and Financial Institutions. In addition to that disciplinary sanction, the National Bank of Cambodia imposes transactional sanctions: an institution failing to comply with the quarterly reporting obligation in Article 10 is liable to a sanction of 1,000,000 riel per day of delay, and an institution failing to comply with this Prakas is liable to a sanction of 3,000,000 riel per day counting from the date the National Bank of Cambodia required it to take corrective action.

chunks.doc: Prakas on Interest Rate Ceiling on Loan (NBC unofficial English translation)
chunks.instrument: Prakas No. B7-017-109 P.K dated 13 March 2017 on Interest Rate Ceiling on Loan
chunks.text: This Prakas applies to microfinance deposit-taking institutions, microfinance institutions, and rural credit operators under the supervisory authority of the National Bank of Cambodia. Those institutions must set the interest at not exceeding 18 per cent per annum for any maturity of loan. The stated objective of the Prakas is to protect consumers from excessive interest rates charged by the institution and to promote the use of affordable loans. The ceiling does not by its terms extend to lenders outside those categories, so a loan from a commercial bank or from an unlicensed lender is not covered by this 18 per cent figure.
chunks._scopeCaution: The final sentence states the limit of Article 3 rather than extending it. Article 3 lists the institutions covered; it does not mention commercial banks. Saying so explicitly matters because a citizen told '18% is the legal cap' would be misled about a bank loan or a moneylender. The Prakas is silent on those, and silence is reported as silence, not as permission or prohibition.

chunks.doc: Prakas on Interest Rate Ceiling on Loan (NBC unofficial English translation)
chunks.instrument: Prakas No. B7-017-109 P.K dated 13 March 2017 on Interest Rate Ceiling on Loan
chunks.text: The interest rate ceiling applies to a new loan contract, including a restructured loan and a refinancing, signed by signature or fingerprint from 1 April 2017. An institution that fails to comply may face disciplinary sanctions under Article 52 of the Law on Banking and Financial Institutions.
